result.title: Movie2Game-Bench: Holistic Evaluation of Film-to-Game Adaptation Beyond Playability
result.summary: Adapting a film into a game requires selecting source elements and translating them into player actions, rules, and feedback. We introduce Movie2Game-Bench (M2G-bench), a benchmark for evaluating film-to-game adaptation beyond playability. M2G-bench combines general evaluation, movie-specific evaluation, and playtesting by three GUI model players. The protocol connects source content to gameplay steps and implementation evidence, capturing both content preservation and interactive realization. The benchmark comprises 22 films and 658 source-specific reference items. Evaluating 14 models on the same films with their selected primary harnesses reveals complementary strengths in game quality, adaptation, and player experience. A shared weakness concerns playable sequences: this category has the lowest content-presence mean in all 14 models, averaging 37.9 out of 100 compared with 54.8 for iconic elements. Among judgments of retained emotionaldevelopment content, narrative choices account for 60.0% and scenario operation for 7.2%. These findings identify two linked priorities for film-to-game adaptation: preserving source situations that can support gameplay and connecting retained content to player actions and consequences.

AI.brief_summary: Movie2Game-Bench 提出电影改游戏改编的评测基准，含 22 部影片、658 条源内容参照项，并把通用评测、影片特定评测与三个 GUI 模型玩家的试玩结合起来，评测 14 个模型；结果显示标志性元素保留尚可，但「可玩序列」类内容存在度最低（均值 37.9）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「内容被保留却未转化为可玩序列」的落差，可能类比 LVR 中视觉细节存在于内部状态却未进入推理与答案；该基准把源内容与玩家动作、后果显式挂钩的评测协议，可供核查 latent 证据是否真正被使用这一评价问题。
